title: Redwood All-Hands - June 2026
summary: Company all-hands covering Q2 highlights (growth in hosted API usage, Dedicated contracts expansion), product roadmap updates (runtime optimizations, RLHF evals, private deployment features), hiring and org changes, and a short Q&A. Leadership emphasized reliability, cost controls, and next steps for cross-functional teams.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~65 minutes
Attendees: Elena Park, Marcus Li, Priya Srinivasan, Jamal Rivera, Avery Chen, Sofia Gomez + ~120 people on the call

[00:00] Elena Park: Hey everyone, welcome to the June all-hands. Thanks for joining, I know it's a busy week. Quick agenda — Q2 highlights, product roadmap update, people/hiring updates, and then Q&A. We'll try to keep it tight.

[00:25] Marcus Li: Quick housekeeping — recording is on, please post questions in the Q&A or drop in #all-hands if you need follow-ups. Also, shoutout to infra for the deploy last night that smoothed out a bunch of p99 noise.

[00:40] Elena Park: Great, starting with the numbers. Q2 we saw a 38% increase in hosted API token volume month-over-month, and Dedicated bookings grew by 22% quarter-over-quarter. Net retention for Dedicated customers improved — small sample but encouraging. Revenue was slightly ahead of plan, driven by two mid-market expansions and one enterprise Dedicated contract that closed late in the quarter.

[01:10] Jamal Rivera: To add, pipeline quality improved — we're seeing more proof-of-concept to committed conversion in finance and healthcare verticals. The Dedicated deals come with specific compliance asks, which is where our Private offering and audit logs are resonating.

[01:35] Elena Park: Important callouts — units economics are holding but we've seen some pressure from high sequence-length workloads. That's a prompt to talk about Optimize and runtime changes. Priya?

[01:50] Priya Srinivasan: Thanks. On roadmap: main focus next quarter is threefold — 1) runtime perf (KV cache improvements, better batching heuristics), 2) product features for Private (simpler VPC setup, improved KMS integrations and audit exporting), 3) developer UX (streaming reliability, better SDK ergonomics). We're also planning to publish more verified performance profiles for models and quantized variants.

[02:25] Avery Chen: Quick technical note — the KV cache change in the branch reduced repeated context cost in our internal benchmarks by about 18% for typical chat workloads. The change is behind a feature flag, we want to ramp slowly to monitor real-world effects.

[02:45] Marcus Li: On the runtime side, we want to prioritize kernel selection improvements for long-sequence attention patterns. We're seeing a mismatch in hardware utilization when customers push >4k tokens. There's a tactical plan: smarter kernel fallbacks and a sequence-length aware scheduler.

[03:10] Elena Park: Nice. On Private and Dedicated: we closed one pilot for a large insurance customer who requested an air-gapped option and enhanced audit logs. That drove our push to make the Private onboarding smoother. We need cross-functional help — SEs, infra, and product to align on a checklist.

[03:35] Jamal Rivera: We're standardizing a checklist in the deals playbook — SSO/SAML requirements, SOC2/ISO requests, KMS/HSM key rotation questions, and network topology considerations. AE/SE should expect a new one-pager to share with customers early next week.

[03:55] Elena Park: Ok people update — Sofia?

[04:05] Sofia Gomez: Hiring highlights: we've hired 12 engineers this quarter, and ramped up SE coverage in EMEA. We still have critical roles open — senior runtime engineers, a privacy/security PM, and a couple of experienced SRE hires. Also, heads up: we'll run the company engagement survey Thursday; please participate, it's short.

[04:30] Elena Park: Great, thanks. A couple of culture notes: first, we're instituting a quarterly hack week in August to surface cost-saving and developer-experience improvements. Second, reminder on our comp and recognition cycle next month, managers will receive guidance on merit increases and leveling.

[04:55] Marcus Li: On reliability and observability, Ops shipped a new per-route latency breakdown in Console last week. It's in beta but a few customers are trialing it. We need more internal adoption to catch edge cases before wider rollout.

[05:15] Priya Srinivasan: Also, we're expanding the evals program to include safety/regression checks tied to prompt sets. The goal is to automatically guard against quality regressions when we switch model variants or roll quantized builds.

[05:35] Audience question (typed): "How are we balancing latency vs cost for Dedicated customers?"

[05:40] Jamal Rivera: Great question. For Dedicated customers the tradeoff is explicit — some want lowest latency and are willing to pay for reserved GPU capacity, others care more about cost and accept higher tail latency. We provide config levers — batch size caps, cold-start policies, and auto-burst — and the SEs recommend profiles per workload.

[06:05] Avery Chen: To add, our Optimize tooling will start suggesting quantization and batching profiles per route next quarter, based on observed traffic patterns. That should reduce unit cost without big quality regressions for many workloads.

[06:25] Audience question: "Any updates on compliance and SOC2 renewals?"

[06:30] Elena Park: We are mid-audit for SOC2 Type II and tracking ISO 27001 readiness. Security's been working closely with the certification firm and customers. If you're in Product or Eng and have outstanding action items from previous audits, check your inbox and the security confluence page.

[06:50] Marcus Li: One operational note — KMS support for external HSM providers is in alpha. We're validating key rotation flows with a partner. Expect more details in the Private onboarding doc.

[07:10] Audience question: "What's the plan for open models vs proprietary models?"

[07:15] Priya Srinivasan: Our strategy is model-agnostic serving — we want to support the best-in-class open models and provide curated, verified options in the catalog. We also plan to support customers who want to run private proprietary fine-tuned checkpoints in Dedicated/Private with the same serving guarantees. The catalog will show perf and cost tradeoffs.

[07:45] Elena Park: Quick customer story — a fintech pilot reduced their per-call latencies by moving from a cold-hosted flow to our Dedicated pool with KV caching turned on; it improved accuracy on long conversations because the cache preserved history.

[08:05] Jamal Rivera: Ok folks, a heads-up on quotas and rate limiting: as usage grows we may tighten free-tier burst limits to protect SLOs. We'll communicate any changes with a 30-day window.

[08:25] Marcus Li: On experimentation — we've started a small A/B rollout for a new streaming buffer algorithm that reduces tail latency at the cost of slightly more memory. We'll monitor memory pressure and customer-facing p95/p99.

[08:45] Audience Q&A segment — mixed questions about remote-work stipends, travel policy, and conference presence. Sofia addressed People Ops items.

[09:10] Sofia Gomez: Travel policy update: we'll reopen conference travel approvals for customer-facing roles with manager sign-off, and we have a modest pool for conference sponsorships. Also, remote-work stipends will be extended to new hires starting July 1st.

[09:35] Audience question: "Will we open another office in APAC?"

[09:40] Elena Park: We are exploring an APAC hub but no decisions yet. We recently expanded cloud region coverage via partners which helps customers in APAC; physical office is longer-term.

[10:00] Priya Srinivasan: Roadmap timeline — expect a public roadmap snapshot in three weeks and a deeper technical RFC for runtime perf in two weeks. We'll use the RFC process to invite cross-team feedback.

[10:20] Marcus Li: Important ask for Eng leads — please review the perf RFC and run the perf harness on any dominos (internal workloads) that might be impacted. We need early adopters to validate traffic characteristics.

[10:40] Short lightning updates from teams (each ~30s): Org Growth, Infra, Product, Sales.

[12:00] Elena Park: Closing remarks — big thanks, this has been a strong quarter but there's work ahead. Focus areas for Q3: operationalizing Private onboarding, hitting our Dedicated commit targets, and continuing to tighten unit economics.

[12:30] Elena Park: Recap of next steps: leadership Q3 doc, product roadmap deck, pulse survey, and SE playbook checklist for Private.

[12:50] Audience: Applause and a few people dropping quick congratulations in chat.

[13:00] End of recording.

Notes about transcript quality: automated captions sometimes garble product names (e.g., "KV cache" as "KV cash"), speaker attribution may be coarse for large attendee count. This transcript preserves timestamps and some disfluency to reflect natural speech.
